points.title: Flowchart
points.must: A diagram showing the steps of one process / algorithm in order, using standard symbols joined by flow lines (arrows).

points.title: Algorithm and process design
points.must: Algorithm = finite sequence of clear steps; process design = planning the logic of every process before coding.

points.title: The flowchart symbols
points.must: Terminator (START/END), process rectangle (calculation), parallelogram (input/output), diamond (decision, two exits), subroutine, flow line — each drawn with an example.

points.title: DFD vs flowchart
points.must: DFD shows what processes exist and how data flows; flowchart shows how one process works, including decisions and loops.

points.title: Advantages and disadvantages
points.must: At least two advantages (visual, errors found before coding, language-independent, documentation) and one disadvantage (large, slow to change).

points.title: Rules for a good flowchart
points.must: One START and an END, top to bottom with arrowheads, two labelled exits per decision, one step per box, correct symbols.

points.title: Sequence, selection, iteration
points.must: The three structures named and described; sequence = steps in order, selection = decision chooses a path.

points.title: Variable and assignment
points.must: A variable is a named storage location; assignment cost ← tickets × 2500 stores a value.

points.title: Sequence flowchart
points.must: A drawn example, e.g. INPUT tickets → cost ← tickets × 2500 → OUTPUT cost.

points.title: Selection flowchart
points.must: A drawn example with a diamond, Yes/No exits that join again (e.g. delivery 0 or 1500).

points.title: Worked example with test values
points.must: Cinema price (under 12 → 1500, otherwise 2500) tested with normal and boundary values (11, 12).

points.title: Nested selection
points.must: Grade from a mark with decisions 85 / 70 / 50 checked from the highest boundary down.

points.title: Conditions and operators
points.must: =, <>, <, <=, >, >=, AND, OR, NOT with examples; range 11–18 written with AND.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Wrong shapes, decision with one exit / unlabelled, wrong boundary (< vs <=), OR instead of AND.
